title: Avalon Insurance - Assurance Posture Review
summary: High-level SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review focused on Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. Customer requested timeline for evidence handoff, clarification on private deployment options for data residency, and a tentative pilot for dedicated capacity to run log-forwarding tests.
topics: Audit logs: retention, export, and schema
Data residency and private deployment options
Next steps: evidence handoff and pilot setup
action_items: Maya Chen - Share SOC 2 Type II report excerpts + access instructions to Trust Center - due 2026-01-14
Evan Ortiz - Draft recommended RBAC role mapping for Avalon (example JSON) and sample audit log export schema - due 2026-01-18
Priya Raman - Provide list of control owners and required evidence buckets by 2026-01-20
Tom Becker - Confirm preferred cloud region(s) for private deployment and data residency constraints - due 2026-01-16
next_steps: Send Trust Center invite with read-only report access
Schedule a follow-up technical deep dive for KMS/BYOK with infra team (Evan + Tom)
Spin up a 2-week dedicated pilot to validate log forwarding and RBAC enforcement
Map control owners to Redwood checklist and align evidence handoff plan
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Maya Chen (AE), Evan Ortiz (SE)
Attendees (Customer): Priya Raman (Head of Security), Tom Becker (Platform Lead), Leah Ortiz (Compliance Manager), Nick (internal auditor)

00:00 Maya: ok, welcome everyone, thanks for making time. we'll run through a posture review for SOC two slash ISO, try to keep to about 45 minutes then leave time for next steps. i sent the agenda earlier, anyone want to add something quick?
00:18 Priya: no, that looks good. primary thing for us is to understand what artifacts you can share, and how we get access to the trust center for our auditors. then second is to confirm how redwood handles key management and whether we can bring our own keys.
00:31 Maya: great, that's exactly what Evan will cover. Evan, do you want to start on trust center and reports?
00:37 Evan: yeah, sure. so first, we provide a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 audit summary in the Trust Center. access can be set as read-only for customer reviewers and auditors. note that some supporting evidence is redacted for third-party confidentiality but we provide control mappings and test results.
00:55 Leah: redacted how — will redactions block our auditor from signing off? last time a vendor withheld some logs and that became an issue.
01:03 Evan: good question. generally we don't redact items that are required to demonstrate control effectiveness. redactions are limited to internal vendor-specific procedural docs. for audit evidence we provide sample traces, anonymized user ids only when necessary, and full control test outputs. if the auditor needs raw data, we can work through an NDA and deeper access for a time-bound window.
01:28 Priya: ok, that'll probably be required. our timeline is locked — audit kickoff in early March. we need evidence packaged by mid-February.
01:36 Maya: understood. we'll include timelines in the follow-up. next, RBAC and SSO. Evan?
01:43 Evan: so redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. for RBAC we have built-in roles and we also support custom role definitions per account. typical pattern for enterprise is to sync groups from IdP and map them to minimum-privilege roles — e.g., auditor, admin, ops, developer.
02:02 Tom: do you support attribute-based access control? we have env/region attributes that we'd like enforced.
02:08 Evan: not full ABAC today, mostly group and role based. you can use attribute tags on resources and the console will show them, but enforcement of attribute-based policies is not first-class. we do have planned work for more granular policies later this year.
02:26 Priya: that's a potential gap for us. our architecture review board needs regional restrictions enforced at the service level. is there a workaround?
02:34 Evan: one pattern is to use separate accounts or projects per region and apply role mappings there. it's more operational overhead but it achieves isolation. we can map that in the controls matrix we share.
02:47 Leah: will SCIM provisioning support mapping of nested groups? our idp has nested groups for auditors.
02:54 Evan: SCIM supports nested group sync for most IdPs; if not, we can script a sync. we'll include an example for Okta and Azure AD in the follow-up.
03:10 Nick: quick on logging — what's the retention window and can we pull raw logs to our SIEM?
03:16 Evan: logs are retained in the hosted plan for 90 days by default; for Dedicated/Private deployments you can configure retention to meet your policies and forward logs to your S3/Blob or SIEM via webhook or syslog bridge. we provide a schema and sample export.
03:32 Tom: for private deployment do you require a full private control plane or can we use VPC peering to keep data in our region?
03:40 Evan: we have both modes. VPC peering with a private control plane is supported in our Private offering; that keeps traffic within your network and allows region residency. on-prem package is available for strict air-gap requirements but that is heavier to operationalize.
03:56 Priya: about KMS, can we BYOK and use our HSM keys?
04:01 Evan: yes, BYOK is supported for customer-managed keys; we integrate with common cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and we also support external HSMs through a connector. keys can be used for data at rest encryption and for disk-level encryption of persistent caches. note: some ephemeral cache keys are managed by runtime but long-term ciphertexts can be under your key.
04:26 Leah: is key rotation automated or manual? our policy requires quarterly rotation with proof of rotation in evidence.
04:33 Evan: rotation is customer-controlled; we provide procedures and scripts to perform key rotation and key rewrap; we'll deliver step-by-step docs and sample logs for evidence.
04:45 Maya: ok circling back to evidence collection — Priya, you said mid-February target. We'll package control mappings and sample evidence sets. what format does your auditor prefer?
04:55 Priya: CSV or spreadsheet mapping control to evidence is fine, and then zipped artifacts for logs and config snapshots. we need chain of custody notes.
05:05 Maya: great. Evan, can you walk through how audit logs look — fields, timestamps, user id locations — so we can check compatibility with Avalon SIEM?
05:14 Evan: sure. typical event includes timestamp (UTC), request id, actor (user or service), principal id, action, resource arn-ish, request payload hash, response code, and pod/node id if on dedicated. we also include session start/stop events for streaming. sample schema will be attached.
05:38 Tom: payload hashes — do you include any PII fields in logs? we try to avoid that.
05:43 Evan: by default we do not log sensitive request bodies; logs are metadata-heavy. if you enable debug traces you might see truncated inputs; those are redacted by default and stored under restricted access.
05:59 Priya: about data residency, if we choose the EU region does Redwood guarantee resident storage for backups and logs?
06:07 Evan: for Private and Dedicated in-region deployments we keep backups and logs in-region. for hosted customers there is geo-routing — EU customers in our EU region have logs and backups stored in EU; we can provide a data residency attestation for contracts.
06:24 Leah: any SLA differences for Private? also question on retention policies — can we set retention to seven years?
06:31 Maya: dedicated contracts can include custom retention and SLA. seven years is unusual but possible if you add object storage retention as part of contract. we'll need to price that.
06:45 Nick: auditor asks about separation of duties — how do you ensure engineers can't access audit logs?
06:51 Evan: RBAC with least privilege, combined with audit trails and canary alerts. we enforce separation in the control plane: only auditors and security ops groups can view raw logs. normal developer roles only see limited telemetry. all access is logged and immutable in the audit trail.
07:10 Priya: can we get an example immutable audit log export for our internal compliance team?
07:16 Evan: yes. we'll provide a sample ndjson export with signatures for immutability markers.
07:25 Maya: i want to put a pin in KMS integration and run a BYOK mock next week with Tom's team. Tom, are you available for a technical session?
07:34 Tom: yes, next Thursday morning works.
07:36 Maya: perfect, we'll schedule.
07:39 Evan: one more point, we have a controls mapping template that maps our product features to common SOC 2/ISO controls. it shows which artifacts are available in the trust center and which require customer-provided evidence.
07:51 Leah: can you flag gaps upfront? we'd like to know which controls are customer responsibilities vs vendor responsibility.
07:57 Evan: absolutely; the matrix has owner columns for vendor/customer and suggested evidence. we'll customize it for Avalon.
08:05 Priya: ok onboarding and next steps — what's the recommended path, quick pilot or full evidence transfer?
08:11 Maya: recommend pilot: a 2-week dedicated pilot to validate log forwarding, RBAC sync and the BYOK flow. meanwhile we'll share reports and the controls matrix to start evidence prep.
08:23 Nick: timeline check — pilot next week, evidence package mid-February, audit kickoff early March — seems tight, are there risks?
08:30 Evan: main risk is time for NDA and temporary auditor access if raw artifacts are needed. also key rotation and integration testing could reveal config drift. we can mitigate by locking down a stubbed dataset for testing.
08:47 Priya: we'll prepare the list of control owners and evidence buckets by Monday.
08:51 Maya: great. any final questions?
08:55 Tom: just SSO proof — do you have SAML metadata files we can test?
08:59 Evan: yes, sample metadata and SCIM endpoints will be included in the follow-up email.
09:06 Leah: thanks, this was helpful.
09:09 Maya: thanks everyone. recap: we'll send Trust Center invite, SOC 2 excerpts, controls matrix; Evan will send RBAC mapping and log schema; schedule KMS deep dive with Tom. action items captured and we'll follow up by Friday.
09:26 [call ends]
